presentingComplaint: Recurrent episodes of severe right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals
history: 44-year-old woman with a 3-month history of intermittent, self-limiting attacks of severe steady right upper quadrant / epigastric pain, typically beginning 30-60 minutes after fatty or heavy meals, lasting 1-3 hours before resolving spontaneously. Pain radiates to the right scapula/interscapular region and is associated with nausea. Attacks are episodic with complete resolution and no symptoms between episodes. No fever, no jaundice, no dark urine or pale stools. Risk factors: female, overweight (BMI 31), two prior pregnancies (multiparous), age in 40s. No prior surgery. No alcohol excess.
examination: Comfortable and afebrile between attacks; during the current attack mild right upper quadrant tenderness on deep palpation without guarding or rebound. Murphy sign NEGATIVE. No palpable mass, no hepatomegaly. No scleral icterus. Bowel sounds normal. No costovertebral angle tenderness.
imaging: Transabdominal ultrasound: multiple mobile echogenic gallstones with posterior acoustic shadowing in the gallbladder; gallbladder wall thickness normal (<3 mm); no pericholecystic fluid; common bile duct normal calibre (4 mm); no intra/extrahepatic ductal dilatation.
citations: Harrison 22e — Diseases of the Gallbladder and Bile Ducts
ACG Clinical Guideline: Management of Gallstone Disease / SAGES Guidelines for Cholecystectomy 2010
contraindications: NSAIDs (e.g., diclofenac for analgesia) contraindicated in peptic ulcer disease, significant renal impairment, or aspirin-sensitive asthma
edgeCases: Prolonged pain (>4-6 hours), fever, or a positive Murphy sign signals progression to acute cholecystitis rather than uncomplicated biliary colic
Deranged LFTs or a dilated CBD suggests choledocholithiasis/cholangitis and warrants MRCP/EUS
expectedMaiK: Classic biliary colic from cholelithiasis: episodic post-prandial RUQ pain that fully resolves, normal inflammatory markers and LFTs, and gallstones without wall thickening on ultrasound. Because it is non-infective, no antibiotics are indicated; management is analgesia and elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for recurrent symptoms.
expectedNextQuestions: Does any single attack last longer than 4-6 hours or is it now accompanied by fever, jaundice, or dark urine (suggesting cholecystitis or CBD stone)?
How frequent and disabling are the attacks (to decide on elective cholecystectomy)?
expectedInvestigations: Liver function tests and lipase to exclude choledocholithiasis/pancreatitis
MRCP or EUS only if LFTs deranged or CBD dilated
regressionAssertions: stewardship tier is null (non-infective condition, no antibiotics)
Murphy sign negative and normal WBC/LFTs distinguish from CHOLECYSTITIS
